rationale: THE BASE HALF of the cross-file `overrides` pin, and it is pinned for its own sake rather than as an accessory. `RealPhpAnalyzer.resolveOverrides` can only verify an override whose base declaration is VISIBLE, and until the M60 round nothing on any test or gate path ever built `AnalyzeContext.overrideCompanion` — so the cross-file path had NO pin at all: no fixture, no mutant, and no differential that could see a wrong target either, because the published match is `(label, target)` through `normTarget`, the LAST SEGMENT, so a truth row naming `TestCase.__construct` is satisfied by any other `__construct` override in the draw. `run-fixtures.ts` now accepts an opt-in `crossFileOverride` key, and this file is the companion source `cross-file-override.php` names. Pinning what the base DECLARES matters because the subclass fixture's forbid rows are only meaningful against a known declaration set: `inheritedOnly` and `neverRedeclared` are here precisely so that 'the base does not declare it' is checkable. The private and protected members are the half that found a real defect — see the subclass file's rationale.

expectSymbols.name: BaseContract
expectSymbols.comment: an abstract base declared in its OWN compilation unit — this file

expectSymbols.name: execute
expectSymbols.comment: redeclared by the subclass across a file boundary: a genuine override

expectSymbols.name: inheritedOnly
expectSymbols.comment: NOT redeclared by the subclass. Inheriting is not overriding, and the cross-file path must be as strict about that as the same-file path.

expectSymbols.name: neverRedeclared
expectSymbols.comment: no subclass declares this, so no override edge may name it

expectSymbols.name: make
expectSymbols.comment: static, and redeclared as static by the subclass, which PHP permits

expectSymbols.name: privateHelper
expectSymbols.comment: PRIVATE. PHP does not inherit a private method, so a subclass method of the same name is a DIFFERENT method. This row is the one that found a real defect — and note that the filter applies to SAME-FILE bases, because that is where identity is exact; for a cross-file base the visibility is knowable only from a name-keyed index, which php's leaf-name model makes ambiguous, so it is deliberately not acted upon. See the subclass fixture's forbid rows.

expectSymbols.name: protectedHelper
expectSymbols.comment: protected, and redeclared protected: a genuine override, and the contrast case that proves the filter is on VISIBILITY rather than on presence
